chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim told me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, who said: Musa ibn Sa'dan al-Hannat told me, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «He knows the secret and what is more hidden». He said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden is what crosses your mind and then you forget.

key_terms.أَخْفَى: More hidden; what crosses the mind and is forgotten
key_terms.أَنْسَيْتَهُ: You forgot it; the state of losing awareness of the thought
key_terms.السِّرّ: The secret; what is consciously concealed in the heart

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between 'the secret' and 'what is more hidden' in Quran 20:7 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchical depth of divine knowledge by distinguishing between conscious concealment ('al-sirr') and fleeting, forgotten thoughts ('wa akhfa'). This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly understanding that Allah’s awareness extends beyond deliberate secrets to include the ephemeral whispers of the mind, reinforcing the concept of comprehensive omniscience.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: I was told by my paternal uncle, Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasim, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Kufi, that he said: I was told by Musa bin Sa’dan, the Wheat Seller, from Abdullah bin Qasim, from Abdullah bin Maskan, from Muhammed bin Muslim, that he said:

I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «He knows the secret and what is more hidden» [20:7]. He said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden is what comes to your mind and then which you forget.
